name: Amrakhand (Mango Yogurt Dessert)

cookwares.name: large cotton dish towel or cheesecloth

ingredients.name: whole nutmeg, finely grated , plus more for serving

instructions.primary_message: Line a large colander with a clean, large 100% cotton dish towel or a triple layer of cheesecloth and set it over a deep bowl or pot, making sure there is enough space beneath the colander for the whey to drain without touching the bottom.

Spoon the yogurt into the center of the towel or cheesecloth. Gather edges of cloth over yogurt and tie tightly with kitchen twine, string, or a strong rubber band to form a sealed pouch. Refrigerate and let drain until thickened, 8 to 10 hours. Discard drained whey or save for another use.
Transfer drained yogurt (chakka) to a large bowl. Measure out 0.91 kg drained yogurt, saving any remaining yogurt for another use. Cover and refrigerate until ready to use.
In a small microwave-safe bowl, heat milk or water until warm, 5 to 10 seconds. Add saffron and let steep until fragrant and deeply colored, 1 to 2 minutes.

In a large bowl, stir drained yogurt with a spatula until smooth and free of lumps, 30 to 60 seconds. Add 6 tablespoons sugar and stir until fully dissolved. Add nutmeg and saffron-milk mixture and stir to combine. Refrigerate until ready to use.

While yogurt mixture is chilling, in a small saucepan, combine mango pulp and remaining 4 tablespoons sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, occasionally stirring and scraping the bottom, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon and a spatula leaves a visible trail across the bottom of the pan, about 5 minutes. Let cool completely, about 15 minutes.
Fold cooled mango mixture into the chilled yogurt mixture until evenly combined and pale orange in color. Top with additional grated nutmeg before serving.

description: This cool, creamy Indian dessert combines tangy strained yogurt with sweet Alphonso mangoes, saffron, and nutmeg for an easy, make-ahead summer treat.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 8 hr 40 min.

Optional substitutions: whole milk → water

Notes: If possible, seek out tangier yogurt varieties like Karoun, Damavand, Abali, or Sadaf—brands often found in South Asian, Iranian, and Middle Eastern grocery stores. Alternatively, add a small splash of fresh lemon juice to plain yogurt to approximate the flavor of traditional South Asian yogurt.

Make-ahead and storage: Yogurt can be drained up to 4 days in advance. Once it has reached the desired consistency (after 8 to 10 hours), transfer it to an airtight container and refrigerate. Do not continue draining, or it can become overly thick, dense, and slightly crumbly as more whey is lost.
The mango pulp mixture can be prepared up to 4 days in advance and refrigerated in an airtight container. Let it cool completely before refrigerating
Amrakhand can be prepared up to 4 days in advance.
Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days in advance.
author: Kaumudi Marathé
